lines.raw: Step 1: the provider dimension.

lines.raw: In a data warehouse, the provider master file becomes a **provider dimension**: one row per provider **version**.
lines.say: In a data warehouse, the provider master file becomes a provider dimension: one row per provider version.

lines.raw: When an important detail like the address changes, we do not overwrite the old row.
lines.say: When an important detail like the address changes, we do not overwrite the old row.

lines.raw: We **close** it with an end date and **add** a new row.
lines.say: We close it with an end date and add a new row.

lines.raw: This is the "keep history" fix from lesson 7, so old claims still show the address that was true at the time.

lines.raw: Step 2: join claims to providers.
lines.say: Step 2: join claims to providers.

lines.raw: Each claim line has **two** provider columns: `billing_npi` and `rendering_npi`.
lines.say: Each claim line has two provider columns: billing_npi and rendering_npi.

lines.raw: So we join the provider table **twice**, once for each role, and we match on the **service date** so we pick the right version of the row:
lines.say: So we join the provider table twice, once for each role, and we match on the service date so we pick the right version of the row:

lines.raw: Billing side: `claim.billing_npi = bill.npi AND claim.from_dt BETWEEN bill.eff_dt AND bill.end_dt`.
lines.say: Billing side: claim.billing_npi = bill.npi A N D claim.from_dt BETWEEN bill.eff_dt A N D bill.end_dt.

lines.raw: Rendering side: `claim.rendering_npi = rend.npi AND claim.from_dt BETWEEN rend.eff_dt AND rend.end_dt`.
lines.say: Rendering side: claim.rendering_npi = rend.npi A N D claim.from_dt BETWEEN rend.eff_dt A N D rend.end_dt.

lines.raw: Use a **left join** on the rendering side, because many hospital lines have no rendering NPI (NULL).
lines.say: Use a left join on the rendering side, because many hospital lines have no rendering N P I (N U L L).
